To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) the effect of the defect model error on failure probability is small and (b) the effect of defect model error on NO measurement interpretation is small and in the opposite direction.
the effect of the defect model error on the failure probability calculation depends on the type and size of the defect model and the type of NO measurement.
the effects of the use of a simplified defect model on the interpretation of NO data and on the prediction of failure probability tend to compensate rather than compound each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sensitivity of the calculation of failure probabilities to errors in the defect modelling.
the sensitivity of the failure prediction to model errors in the defect geometry and in the measurement interpretation procedure.
a theoretical study of the sensitivity of the probability of failure to errors in the defect modelling used in NO interpretation and in failure probability calculation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no general statement that can be made about the sensitivity of failure prediction to model error.
the errors of the defect models used in NO measurements and in failure probability calculation are not necessarily additive.
the effects of model errors in the failure probability calculation are not very sensitive to the model errors in the NO measurements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the errors due to oversimplified models are not large and that the errors in measurement interpretation and in failure probability calculations tend to compensate for each other.
the effects of defect model errors are not always the same in the interpretation of the measurement data and in the calculation of the failure probabilities.
, in general, the errors in the interpretation of the synthetic NO measurements tend to be smaller than those in the failure probability calculation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the errors in failure probability calculations due to errors in defect modelling are not necessarily large and may in some cases be small.
the effects of the two types of errors tend to compound.
in many cases the effects of the model errors tend to cancel each other.
